source_text: in spiritu praevidentes, ista dixerunt; sed apertius Ieremias: In diebus illis, inquit, non dicent: Patres manducaverunt uvam acerbam, et dentes filiorum obstupuerunt, sed unusquisque in suo peccato morietur; et eius qui manducaverit uvam acerbam, ostupescent dentes ipsius
pass_a_gloss: In spiritu praevidentes, that dixerunt; but apertius Ieremias: in diebus those, he-says, not dicent: Patres manducaverunt uvam acerbam, and dentes filiorum obstupuerunt, but unusquisque in his-own by-sin morietur; and his/its who manducaverit uvam acerbam, ostupescent dentes of-himself.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: The proverb will no longer be used which says that parents ate sour grapes and their children’s teeth were set on edge. A son will not die for his father’s sin, nor a father for his son’s sin; the soul that sins will itself die. (Ezekiel 18:2–4,20)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
